headline: US stocks closed higher in shortened Black Friday session as AI and semiconductor rebound drove indexes to strongest weekly gains since 2025
raw_text:
- S&P 500 ($SPX) rose 1.60% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) gained 2.31% to 24,129.50, the Dow Jones ($DJI) added 591.99 points (1.18%) to 50,774.94, and the Russell 2000 (IWM) advanced 1.71% to 2,750.30
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) booked a 5.6% weekly advance, its strongest since April 2025, while the Dow logged its best week since 2022
- Semiconductors led with the SOX index up 4.69% as Micron Technology (MU) rose 7.60%, Sandisk (SNDK) jumped 15.96%, Marvell Technology (MRVL) gained 7.34%, Coherent (COHR) climbed 14.07% after a director disclosed a $34.7 million open-market stock purchase, AMD (AMD) added 4.56%, and Intel (INTC) advanced 5.38%
- Amazon.com (AMZN) gained 3.96% on early Black Friday sales data and AI initiatives, while Tesla (TSLA) rose 5.22%
- Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) fell 5.24% after the FDA extended its review of IgA nephropathy drug povetacicept by three months
- All 11 S&P 500 ($SPX) sectors advanced, led by technology with a roughly 2.8% gain
- New home sales surged 14.2% in the latest report, supporting the broader equity advance
- In after-hours trading, Direct Digital Holdings (DRCT) saw limited earnings-related moves while small-cap LAES (LAES) jumped over 20% and Nvidia (NVDA) and Intel (INTC) traded slightly lower without major index impact
- US wholesale inventories, retail inventories, and the trade balance were released today at 8:30 AM ET, offering further macro signals
